title: Count Fancy Numbers in a Range
summary: Given two integers l and r, count the number of integers in the range [l, r] that are either good (digits form a strictly monotone sequence) or have a sum of digits that is good.
statement: Given two integers l and r, count the number of integers in the range [l, r] that are either good (digits form a strictly monotone sequence) or have a sum of digits that is good. A sequence is strictly increasing if each digit is greater than the previous one, and strictly decreasing if each digit is less than the previous one. All single-digit numbers are considered good.
constraints: A number is good when its decimal digits are strictly increasing or strictly decreasing; one digit is good.
A number is fancy when it is good or its digit sum is good; count fancy values in the inclusive range.
hints: Digit DP can track whether the built digits remain increasing, decreasing, undecided, or already invalid.
Also carry the digit sum so an invalid number can still qualify through its sum at the end.
Count valid positive integers up to each bound using tight and started flags, then subtract prefix counts.
The state records exactly the monotonicity history; the terminal union implements “number good or digit sum good,” and prefix subtraction gives the inclusive interval.

tests.explanation: Eight and nine are one-digit good numbers; ten has digit sum one, also good, so all three qualify.
Digits 1<4<5 are strictly increasing, so 145 is fancy.
